---
title: Service
description: pouryakit-service, one Module in a Host of its own process, receiving another Host's Integration Events and Snapshots over RabbitMQ.
---

## What it is

`pouryakit-service` generates the composition the [Proving Sample](/docs/reference/glossary#proving-sample)'s `Inventory.Host` runs: the Inventory [Module](/docs/reference/glossary#module) alone, in a [Host](/docs/reference/glossary#host) with its own database, receiving what Catalog publishes in another Host over a RabbitMQ broker. It holds the Host, its service defaults, Inventory, `Catalog.Contracts` for what it receives, and a smoke test.

<Callout type="warn" title="A Host that receives needs its broker">
  The service always joins RabbitMQ, on `ConnectionStrings:broker`, under the service name the template derives from `-n`. Start it before the Host that publishes: a message published before the service's queue exists on the broker reaches no queue of it.
</Callout>

## When to use it

When you split a Module out of a modular monolith into a process of its own, as Inventory is split out in the Proving Sample. Inside one Host, keep the Module in the modular monolith: [In-process or RabbitMQ](/docs/decision-guides/in-process-or-rabbitmq) weighs the two.

## Generate and run it

<Steps>
<Step>

### Generate it

```bash title="Terminal"
dotnet new pouryakit-service -n Acme.Stock
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Give it PostgreSQL and a broker

Its `appsettings.json` names the database `inventory` and the broker `amqp://guest:guest@localhost:5672/`. It migrates Inventory alone, with `InventoryDbContext`, and its launch profile listens on ports 7081 and 5081, so it runs beside a monolith or a modular monolith. [Running the generated Host](/docs/capabilities/templates#running-the-generated-host) has the PostgreSQL and migration commands; the broker is any RabbitMQ that connection string reaches.

</Step>
<Step>

### Publish from another Host

The publishing Host configures `ConnectionStrings:broker` and a service name of its own; a product Catalog creates there opens its stock item here. [A Host that receives](/docs/capabilities/rabbitmq#a-host-that-receives) shows what the service declares to receive it.

</Step>
</Steps>

## What it composes

| | Stated in |
| --- | --- |
| Only what the service needs: no Catalog, monolith Host or [Reverse proxy](/docs/reference/glossary#reverse-proxy) | [The service](/docs/capabilities/templates#the-service) |
| `Receive` and `ReceiveSnapshot` for Catalog's three wire names | [The service](/docs/capabilities/templates#the-service) |
| One read, the stock item, to an authenticated caller of its [tenant](/docs/reference/glossary#tenant) | [The service](/docs/capabilities/templates#the-service) |
| Delivery between the two Hosts, proven with both running as processes | [The service](/docs/capabilities/templates#the-service) |

## Failure messages

<Accordions>
  <Accordion title="A subscription to an event no Module of the Host publishes">
    Without its `Receive` declaration, the Host fails when it is built: the subscription's type has no wire name here, and the refusal names `Receive`.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Nothing arrives">
    The wire name on `Receive` must be the publishing Module's, character for character. A misspelt one binds the queue to an exchange nobody publishes to, and no check across Hosts can see it.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>
